title: The best to their families
hook: wonderful in public, tired at home, and a hadith that turns the measure around

segments.voice: Yesterday, the verse in al-Rum, and your line: dwell in tranquillity. Did you take a breath at the door? Today, a sentence that measures a person by how they are at home. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-one.

Some people are wonderful in public. Patient with strangers, generous at work, the easiest person at any gathering. Then they get home, and the patience has been spent somewhere else. Short answers. A closed door. A hadith in Jami' at-Tirmidhi takes that pattern and turns the measure around. It doesn't ask how a person is at the mosque, or the office, or online. It asks about the people who see them tired, hungry, and in their oldest clothes.
screen: `WONDERFUL IN PUBLIC.` → `SPENT BY THE TIME THEY'RE HOME.` → `THE MEASURE, TURNED AROUND.`

segments.voice: The hadith, in paraphrase: the best of you are those who are best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says it about himself, and sets home as the measure. The word for family here is ahl: your household, your people. Second, a story of how that works, in Sahih al-Bukhari. The companion Salman al-Farisi visits his brother in faith, Abu al-Darda', and finds Abu al-Darda's wife, Umm al-Darda', looking neglected. She tells him, in paraphrase: your brother has no need of this world. Abu al-Darda' is fasting, and at night he means to pray straight through. Salman makes him eat. When night comes, he tells him to sleep, and late in the night wakes him, and they pray together. Then Salman says, in paraphrase: your Lord has a right over you, your own self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, so give each one its due. When they tell the Prophet, he answers: Salman has spoken the truth. Third, notice whose concern starts the story. A wife, whose husband's devotion had left no room for her. The hadith takes her side, and it does it in the name of worship, not against it. Fourth, what best looks like. Not grand. Eating together. Sleeping enough to be kind in the morning. Giving the people at home the patience you'd give a guest. Another hadith in at-Tirmidhi, in paraphrase: the most complete of the believers in faith are the best of them in character, and the best of you are the best to their wives. Character, measured at the kitchen table.
screen: `THE BEST OF YOU: BEST TO THEIR FAMILY.` · `SALMAN VISITS ABU AL-DARDA'.` · `GIVE EACH ONE ITS DUE.` · `CHARACTER, AT THE KITCHEN TABLE.`

segments.voice: The practice: do something for family. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the people at home, or the family you have, near or far. Who has seen you at your most tired lately? Pick one small thing you can do for them today: a meal, a call, a chore done before anyone asks, or a stretch of full attention with nothing else in your hands. If you pray, you can make the intention for it now. If you don't, just decide it, and picture their face when it happens. The bell holds the time.
The best to their families. A hadith that measures a person at home, among the people who see them tired. Today's word.
screen: `THE BEST TO THEIR FAMILIES — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: best at home. Today, give someone at home the patience you'd give a guest. Tomorrow, home life. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-one.

howItsDone: Muslims cite the hadith "the best of you are the best to their families" when speaking of marriage and home, and teachers use Salman's words to Abu al-Darda' to say that worship should not crowd out the rights of family.

fork.setup: you're Salman, visiting your friend Abu al-Darda'. he's fasting, he means to pray all night, and his wife looks neglected. what do you do?
options: praise his devotion and leave him to it.
eat with him, send him to sleep, and remind him his family has a right over him.
tell his wife to be patient with him.
fork.reveal: Salman made him eat and sleep, prayed with him late in the night, and said: give each one its due. the Prophet said: Salman has spoken the truth.

trapdoor: what you thought: be nice to your family.
what it means: home is where a person is measured: the best are best to their families, and family has a right even beside worship.

what a scholar hears: 'the best of you are the best to their families' (Tirmidhi), Salman's 'give each one its due' confirmed by the Prophet (Bukhari), and 'the best of you are the best to their wives' (Tirmidhi).

sources.ref: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3895 (the best of you are the best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family)

Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1162 (the most complete in faith are the best in character; the best of you are the best to their wives)
